prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: photorealistic 3D game environment art-direction reference, NOT a runtime screenshot.
Primary request: redesign Catch and Run's compact working harbor to look convincingly real, suitable as a Blender modeling and Unreal lighting target.
Style: photorealistic architectural/location photography, physically credible construction and material response, contemporary working port, cinematic but legible late-afternoon coastal light. Muted navy, oxidized red, galvanized steel, weathered timber and warm off-white. Real human scale, crisp mid-scale detail and subtle edge wear. No cartoon, no toy diorama, no painterly stylization, no oversaturated teal-orange filter.
Constraints: existing playable footprint and openings take priority. All stairs, decks, roofs and railings have believable load-bearing connections. Keep circulation open; dress margins, not combat routes. No people, weapons, HUD, reticles, UI, logos or watermark. No giant new landmarks, yachts or city. No floating disconnected objects. Glass must have visible frame depth and a view into real interiors. Rain-darkening only near wet zones; most inland paving is dry. Maintain readable shadows, not crushed-black interiors.
Input images: Image 1 is the authoritative map composition reference only, not a style to imitate. Remove every game overlay.
Composition: one high-resolution wide landscape establishing view of the entire small rectangular harbor island, same three-quarter aerial view as reference, island fills 80% of frame. Keep the dominant low-gabled red warehouse in the middle, worker house and garden at image left, Ferris wheel and timber promenade on the near-left shore, working boats along near seawall, stacked containers and small market on right, crane and unfinished building at far-left rear, low operations buildings along far edge, rescue watchtower/service canopy near right foreground. Preserve this adjacency; do not expand into a town.
Enhancement: warehouse standing-seam roof with sensible skylights, layered gutters, properly supported exterior stair; recessed façades, real door/window reveals; detailed corrugated containers with corner castings; mature wind-shaped coastal trees with natural leaf silhouettes; a lived-in but orderly promenade with café awnings; five modest working boats with shaped hulls, cabins, ropes, tire fenders, clear decks.
Water and sky: believable sea horizon under a pale clouded sky, continuous atmosphere without dark horizon bands. Small wind ripples, broad slow swells, narrow intermittent white wash meeting stained concrete seawall, darker wet tidal band and algae restricted to waterline, not surf flooding the island. Subtle foam around piles and hulls. No giant waves.
Do not tilt-shift or blur the model into a miniature. High detail landscape composition.

Input images: Image 1 establishes existing storefront proportions and centered entrance. Image 2 establishes interior aisle arrangement, rear refrigerators and circulation. These are game blockout references to redesign realistically, not styles to imitate.
Composition: a premium two-panel architectural concept sheet, two equally large stacked wide-angle photographs, narrow clean separator. TOP: near eye-level three-quarter exterior photograph of Harbor Market with seawall behind, full façade and pavement visible. BOTTOM: eye-level view just inside the doorway looking down existing aisle toward refrigerator wall. No inset or diagram.
Keep this a small 14 by 10 meter single-story harbor convenience shop, not a luxury supermarket. Preserve a 3 meter clear centered automatic sliding entrance, flat accessible roof and side maintenance access. Avoid thick opaque window panels.
Exterior: convincing anodized dark aluminum mullions, recessed clear glass, slim ceramic/painted-metal fascia, warm cutout letters reading exactly "HARBOR MARKET", restrained white linear sign lighting. Salt traces on lower façade, timber slat accents, concrete curb, drainage channel, a few delivery crates neatly to the side, bicycle rack and bench outside the entrance route. Real glazing reflections without obscuring the shop inside.
Interior: practical suspended ceiling with ventilation grilles and sensible diffused LED light, ceiling neither cavernous nor glaring. Off-white tile with fine grout and faint wear, believable gondola shelving and checkout counter. A varied but organized selection of unbranded packaged snacks, drinks, fruit and household supplies with real packaging silhouettes, paper price strips, fridge door gaskets/handles and subdued condensation, coffee point near checkout. Keep aisle clear and shelves at plausible height. Local scuffs beneath shelving, not uniform dirt everywhere.
Readability: both photos are highly detailed and convincingly real, matching light and architecture between panels. No extra title text.

Input images: Image 1 is the warehouse/container adjacency and scale reference. Image 2 is the construction structure and walkable route reference. Image 3 is the operations interior floorplan reference. These are geometric references, not rendering styles to imitate.
Composition: a clean 2 by 2 contact sheet of four highly detailed eye-level environment photographs, narrow dark separators, no captions. Each photograph must be large and readable.
Top left: the red central warehouse's broad open loading entrance, steel frame, properly supported shallow loading canopy, legible "OLD HARBOR" sign above it. Corrugated cladding with realistic panel scale, bolted galvanized bays, downpipes, dock bumpers, pallets stored at edges. Glimpses of interior shelving and supported catwalks. Preserve the shallow gabled roof and existing exterior roof access stair.
Top right: the harbor construction site, existing concrete skeleton and scaffold, human-scale columns with formwork joints, tie holes and connected rebar cages, slab edge rails, base jacks resting on sole boards, believable crane in background. A clear ground passage under the slabs, stacked timber and steel in existing storage edges, not obstructing the route.
Bottom left: marine engineering operations workshop inside the existing high service hall. Existing open doors and spiral stair, work benches, tool cabinets and consoles refined into convincing real equipment. Supported cable trays, conduits, task lights, lower painted blockwork, softly lit ceiling trusses and dust only at corners. No science-fiction lab.
Bottom right: the existing compact container yard next to Harbor Market. Rust-red, teal and navy shipping containers with recognizable corner castings, deep door reveals, locking bars, practical label plates, localized dents and oxidation. Readable stacking at about 2.5m and 5m with the existing climbing routes, secure interfaces and unobstructed freight lane. No extra stacks beyond the reference area.
All four images share coherent late afternoon coastal lighting and exposure, no monochrome clay renders.

Input images: Image 1 fixes worker house, pond, bridge and garden relationships. Image 2 fixes ticket booth and Ferris wheel arrangement. Image 3 fixes the working fleet's positions, scale and deck envelopes. These guide geometry and layout, not style.
Composition: a polished three-panel environment concept sheet: one wide photograph across the top, two equally sized photographs across the bottom, narrow separators and no captions.
Top: eye-level harbor keeper's house and coastal garden. Keep the two-storey 10 by 8m house and open loggia, traversable openings and pond crossing. Articulate lime-plaster walls with local salt stains, timber recessed windows, real roof tiles/flashing, gutters and eaves. Natural fine-scale leaves and wind-shaped branches instead of giant rounded leaf clumps. Existing planted edges get varied grass and reeds; pond has visible submerged stones, believable dark depth and restrained reflections. Keep paths unobstructed and the Ferris wheel in the background.
Bottom left: restored modest waterfront amusement pier. The existing ticket booth is a real small timber/painted-steel kiosk with framed clear transaction glass, visible inside desk, a working side door and sign "HARBOR TICKETS". Ferris wheel shows bearing housings, hub joints, cabin brackets and restrained lamps; preserve its eight open-front cabins and steel structure.
Bottom right: close eye-level working-boat and quay view. Preserve the small fleet's size and deck clearances but give hulls believable sheer and chine transitions, thick gunwales, recessed wheelhouse windows, welded trim, cleats, secured ropes and worn rubber fenders. Anti-slip deck and sensible shallow cockpit. Clear place for a person to land on deck. Small wind ripples, reflected light, narrow foam along stained seawall and piling bases; water remains below the dry deck, no huge surf, no decorative spray in the walking route. Not yachts and not floating boxes.
Unify all panels through natural material scale, plausible joinery and restrained wear, not excessive grunge.

Composition: two wide photographs stacked vertically, equal panel sizes, narrow separator, no captions.
Top: propose a compact 14 by 14m coastguard rapid-response depot at the existing Hunter release footprint. Keep the broad release gate and unobstructed deployment approach. Real insulated metal door leaves open along grounded guide tracks, substantial frame, warning light housings, navy lower walls and warm off-white upper panels, inset dispatch glazing. Through the opening see a few equipment lockers and a functional preparation bench against the perimeter walls, clear central muster space. Concrete threshold, drainage and restrained deployment markings. No full-size helicopter squeezed into the small footprint, no fantastical bunker or sci-fi laboratory.
Bottom: the rescue maintenance quay from image 2, now physically convincing. Keep the existing elevated watchtower and service canopy locations. Properly braced supports with base plates, steel stair/ladder fittings, lookout glazing and discreet antenna. Under the canopy a rescue inflatable boat on a believable cradle, secured equipment storage and a compact service trolley. Marked open maintenance bay, flush drains, hose reel mounted to structure, rescue rings and mooring fixtures at the quay edge. Add detail to assembly and work surfaces, not random boxes throughout the apron.
Bright coastal late afternoon, some warm practical light, continuous natural sea horizon, clear long walking lanes in both photographs.
